narrative.overview:
An engraving house's page in a night room: dark ink on warm paper, under a near-black cool ground, with one brass lamp for "play this, now" (`docs/research/urtext.md` is the binding spec). The score is always dark ink on paper, in both modes; the highway beneath it is the one dark field, and it is lit only to report state (the awaited note, a hit, a miss). There are no points, ranks, lives or fireworks, and the shell never scores you. The shell around the stage is native-feeling iPadOS (segmented switch, sliders, rows, a drawer) and stays quiet; Newsreader announces and names the music, the system font does the rest. Two modes: Nocturne (dark, the default) and Matinée (light, warm stone). Reading drills reuse the same room with the stage turned down: the staff takes the screen and the highway shrinks to a strip.

The product name is **Page to Hand**: notation on the page becoming understood movement in the player's hands. The Pause / Lid mark and the Urtext visual system are unchanged; the wordmark uses the same Newsreader construction.

The iPad in landscape is the main screen, a desktop browser the second. The player sits 1-2 m away with busy hands, so state is carried by word, shape, and hue together, never hue alone, and every target is thumb-sized on a coarse pointer. Density is moderate and fixed: a 56px top bar, one view, a docked transport. One control height (40px, 44px on touch) and four radii run through the whole shell. Seven tabs live in the top bar until a piece opens: Today, Songs, Read, Scales, Theory, Technique, Progress. Today is a generated plan, not a menu. Progress is the reward: accuracy over time, mastery, a quiet day streak.
keyCharacteristics: A near-black cool ground (warm stone in Matinée) with one warm voice, the lamp brass, that means only "play this / now". Everything else in the shell is neutral Ink.
Newsreader for what is announced and for the names of music; the system font for what is read.
Glow is a state signal on the staff and stage only. No hard offset shadows, no hard text-shadows.
Every page shares one measure and one head; plan rows, song rows and stage rows are one grammar.
Touch first: `pointer: coarse` raises controls to 44px. The app has no minimum width: portrait and split-view windows reflow (see Responsive).
Skill over points: progress is shown as charts, meters and words that can honestly fall; nothing is scored against you and nothing is locked.
Copy is label, value, nothing else.
One dialog grammar (`dialog.sheet`), one tag style, one disclosure marker.

rules.name: The Neutral Progress Rule
rules.body: Mastery and effort are measured in Ink, not in a judgement hue: meter and mastery-cell fill is Ink Soft, and Ink once solid; a practised day is an Ink dot. State is also stated in words ("Solid", "7 of 12 seen") and as a percentage.

rules.name: The Calm Staff Rule
rules.body: The score is Paper Ink on Paper (`--paper-ink` on `--paper`, staff lines `--paper-line`), in both modes. Colour appears on a staff glyph only as state, and every state also has a shape or a word: Paper Cursor for the cursor and Paper Awaited for the notehead being waited for; a grade colour for the 0.8s flash of a hit (`--paper-perfect`, `--paper-great`, `--paper-good`), then the chord settles to Paper Played (a colour change, not a fade, so its grade mark stays at full strength). The grade lives on in a shape under the head, readable with no hue: perfect none (a clean note just goes quiet), great a filled dot, good a filled triangle pointing the way the key missed the beat (◂ early, ▸ late, centred under the head), late an outlined right-pointing triangle, miss a crimson `--paper-miss` cross (the head flashes crimson, then settles to played). A hold outline is the one state that stays on the head: released early a solid crimson outline, held too long a dashed neutral one. Aids that are not score (ghost notes, the Technique aim-for dynamics, 8va brackets, the Dense hint, bar numbers, chord symbols, fingering numbers, the dots of a Ghost of last run) are Paper Ink at 72% or 60% (`--paper-ink-2`, `--paper-ink-3`, mixed on `#staff`); the notes the app plays in accompaniment are the same heads at 50% (3.4:1 on paper; 40% was under 3:1). The score's own marks (articulation, slurs, hairpins, dynamic letters) are Paper Ink at 70%. No glow on paper: light on a page would be a lie.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Amber means "play this, now": the verb and the now-markers. It is never chrome, never selection, never the focus ring, never a link, never text selection, never a judgement grade. Those belong to the Accent. Counted per screen: at most one lamp-filled button, and the lamp Next word only on that button's row. A page with nothing left to do (every plan row done) shows none. On the play screen the dock Play is the one fill; the cursor, awaited heads, receptor lamps and count-in are its now-markers.

rules.name: The Accent Rule
rules.body: Slate blue (#78a9ff; #0058d0 in Matinée) is the interface's own tint and has four jobs: the focus ring, the selected state, links, and text selection. It is never on the staff or in the lanes, never a fill larger than a control, and never the only sign of a state (a selected control also has its raised fill).

rules.name: The Semantic Hue Rule
rules.body: Hand colours (terracotta; verdigris with its lighter edge) and judgement colours (mint, pale mint, neutral, crimson) appear only where a hand or a grade is being reported, never as chrome, decoration, selection or emphasis. Chrome that needs a tint takes Accent Slate or Ink. A chart of grades does not borrow a hand hue either: the Read strip runs neutral to crimson, not the right hand's colour to red.

rules.name: The Word And Shape Rule
rules.body: A judgement colour never stands alone; it ships with its glyph (● ○ ▲ ▸ ×) or its word, and on the staff a position or mark. Hands are told apart by fill style, not hue alone.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: (was Announce Versus Read). Newsreader versus the system font. Newsreader is for what is announced (page titles, the results figure and verdict, the count-in numeral, judgement words, the dock's Play) and for the names of music (piece titles on rows, cards, the start card, the play screen's top title). It is upright and in sentence case, never tracked capitals; the one italic is the staff's own expression words (below). A piece's name inside a sentence or a row of mixed names (Today's plan rows, "Bars 3 to 5 of ...", the Progress ladder) sits in a `.pn` span, which takes Newsreader 560 at 1.1em and the row's ink. Everything tapped or read, and every counter, is the system font in sentence case: section and sheet titles (600, 18 to 22px), labels (600 13px), controls, sentences, the HUD, the tempo, the timers.

rules.name: The Glow Means State Rule
rules.body: A glow is allowed only on an element reporting live state in its own colour. Chrome does not glow.

rules.name: The Soft Shade Rule
rules.body: Nothing carries a hard offset shadow or a hard text-shadow, including the primary button. Separation is a border, a tonal step, or a soft Shade.

rules.name: The One Measure Rule
rules.body: Every non-play page shares the same padding, the 1100px column, and the same page head. No page invents its own left edge.

rules.name: The Plan Rows Share Songs Grammar Rule
rules.body: A plan row, a song row, a stage row and a path row are one row: optional lead, name over sub-line, optional meter, one action at the right, one primary per view. Rows take the cards' 20px inset (`.plan .prow`, the Path's `.rq`, and the Read and Scales stage tables above 760px), so a name starts at the same x on every page. A row's action is ghost unless it is the view's one primary.

rules.name: The Touch Floor Rule
rules.body: Targets are 40px with a fine pointer and 44px with a coarse one; sizes come from `--control`, not literals.

rules.name: The Dialog Sheet Rule
rules.body: Every modal is `dialog.sheet`: header with close, scrolling body, and a pinned footer only when there is an action besides closing (never a second Close). One primary at most, in the footer; three footer actions at most, the rest in the header's ⋯ More. No modal invents its own frame.

rules.name: The Tag Rule
rules.body: A tag is one outlined Ink Soft Label word. Only Next drops the outline (Ink, not lamp), and only on the row with the primary; a page whose head carries Start has none. Tags never use a hand or judgement hue.

rules.name: The One Marker Rule
rules.body: Every disclosure uses the same +/− marker in Ink Faint.

rules.name: The Quiet Bar Rule
rules.body: Chrome fades during a run and returns on any input; it never carries information the player needs mid-run.

dos: **Do** keep notation Ink on Panel and let it ignite only for state.
**Do** pair every judgement colour with a word or position.
**Do** differentiate hands by hue, fill style (solid vs. tinted with a lighter outline) and lane edge.
**Do** reserve Lamp (#ffc83d) for the verb and the now-markers, and use the 2px/2px Accent focus ring everywhere.
**Do** draw control borders in Edge (#727a8b), a floating surface's in Line Strong, and keep Line for hairlines.

**Do** use Ink 2, not Ink 3, for text read mid-song (HUD captions, bar numbers, dock labels, scrub labels): Ink 3 is 5.9:1 and Apple asks 7:1 for small dark-mode text. Ink 3 stays for icons, grabbers and menus read at arm's length.
**Do** keep the staff at print size (staff space about 1.9 mm); the divider's 26% minimum guards it.
**Do** build controls from `--control` and the four radii (6, 10, 14, pill) so touch sizing follows.
**Do** start every non-play page with the page head and the 1100px measure.
**Do** write plan, song and stage rows in the same row grammar.
**Do** build every modal as `dialog.sheet`; header with close, scrolling body, a pinned footer when there is an action besides closing.
**Do** mark every disclosure with the shared +/− marker.
**Do** show tags as outlined Ink Soft words; only Next is plain Ink with no outline, on the primary's row.

**Do** use Newsreader (upright, sentence case) for what is announced and for names of music, and the system font for everything read or tapped; repeat `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on any counter whose rule uses the `font` shorthand (`src/css.test.ts` lists the counters and fails if one loses it; add a new counter to that list).
**Do** mirror any new colour in `src/palette.ts` if Pixi draws it.
**Do** show mastery and effort as Ink meters, cells, charts and dots plus a number or word.
**Do** collapse CSS motion under `prefers-reduced-motion`; on the canvas the hit glow fades at one size and the waiting ring and ghost key hold steady (Calm is the only tier).
donts: **Don't** add glow on chrome, or a frosted-glass imitation.
**Don't** add a hard offset shadow or a hard text-shadow; use Shade.
**Don't** colour notation permanently; colour is a transient state.
**Don't** use amber for focus, selection, links, switches, slider thumbs, the Pause / Lid mark in the bar or the HUD numerals, and never for a judgement grade.
**Don't** use `backdrop-filter`, or an Accent fill larger than a control.
**Don't** reuse a hand or judgement colour for chrome (the on-screen keys, a chart of grades, a connection dot).
**Don't** set text dimmer than Ink Faint (#8a90a0) on Panel, or smaller than 12px.
**Don't** invent a second dialog layout, an inline-styled modal or a coloured tag.
**Don't** put a Label-style kicker above a heading.
**Don't** add paragraphs, parentheticals or explanatory sentences to controls, headers or drawers.
**Don't** show points, ranks, lives, a score or a loss-framed counter; effort only goes up. The day streak is the one counter allowed, small, absent at zero, with freezes.
